- When sentiment is negative (especially > -0.5) and forecast is rising sharply, reduce forecast by 5–10% to avoid overcorrection.  
- If forecast peaks sharply after a recent spike and sentiment is neutral or slightly positive, cap the peak at 1–2% below the immediate prior high.  
- When sentiment is consistently negative over 3+ days, model tends to overcorrect downward — adjust forecast downward by 2–5% relative to prior 30d mean.  
- If forecast is significantly above true outcome for 3+ consecutive days, apply a “mean reversion” correction: subtract 1–3% of the forecasted value from the next 3–5 days.  
- For horizon > 14 days, forecast tends to overestimate downward trend — reduce forecast by 1–3% per 7-day window if sentiment is negative.  
- If sentiment turns positive after a negative streak, model often underreacts — increase forecast by 1–3% for next 3–5 days to capture sentiment shift.
